novel.definition: A printed and bound book that is an extended work of fiction.
novel.exampleUsage: She borrowed a novel about a family adventure.

picture-book.definition: A book in which pictures are a major part of the story or information, often written for children.
picture-book.exampleUsage: The child chose a picture book.

reference-book.definition: A book used to look up facts, such as a dictionary or encyclopedia.
reference-book.exampleUsage: She checked a reference book to confirm the date.

comic-book.definition: A book or magazine that tells stories mainly through sequences of drawings and speech or caption text.
comic-book.exampleUsage: The library has a shelf of comic books.

magazine.definition: A thin publication with articles and pictures, released regularly.

newspaper.definition: A daily or weekly publication on folded sheets.

encyclopedia.definition: A book containing information about many subjects.
encyclopedia.exampleUsage: He used an encyclopedia to learn about planets.

atlas.definition: A collection of maps in book form.
atlas.exampleUsage: She opened the atlas to find a map of Africa.

biography.definition: An account of the series of events making up a person's life.
biography.exampleUsage: He read a biography of a famous scientist.

poetry-book.definition: A book containing poems by one or more writers.

reading-table.definition: A table provided for people to sit and read books or documents.
reading-table.exampleUsage: Students shared a large reading table.

study-desk.definition: A desk intended for quiet studying, reading, or writing.
study-desk.exampleUsage: He worked at a study desk near the window.

bean-bag.definition: A soft seat shaped by loose filling inside a fabric cover.
bean-bag.exampleUsage: Children sat on bean bags in the reading area.

step-stool.definition: A small stool with one or two steps, used to reach high shelves.
step-stool.exampleUsage: The librarian used a step stool to reach the top shelf.

cart.definition: A wheeled frame used to move books and other items around a library.
cart.exampleUsage: The librarian pushed a cart of books between the shelves.

computer-desk.definition: A desk equipped or designed for a computer and related accessories.
computer-desk.exampleUsage: The computer desk had a monitor and keyboard.

armchair.definition: A comfortable chair with arms for one person.
armchair.exampleUsage: She sat in an armchair to read by the window.

fiction.definition: A literary work based on the imagination and not necessarily on fact.
fiction.exampleUsage: The fiction shelves contain made-up stories.

non-fiction.definition: Writing about real people, true events, and facts, not made-up stories.
non-fiction.exampleUsage: He chose a non-fiction book about birds.

children-s-section.definition: An area of a library containing books and services intended for children.
children-s-section.exampleUsage: The children's section has picture books and small tables.

reference-section.definition: A library area containing reference works such as dictionaries, encyclopedias, and atlases, often for use inside the library.
reference-section.exampleUsage: The encyclopedia is in the reference section.

periodicals.definition: Magazines and newspapers published regularly, such as every week or month.
periodicals.exampleUsage: The newest periodicals are displayed near the entrance.

media-center.definition: A room with books, computers, and other media for learning and research.
media-center.exampleUsage: The students used computers in the media center.

study-room.definition: A quiet, tidy room where people study, read, and finish schoolwork.

return-desk.definition: A library counter where borrowed materials are returned or processed.
return-desk.exampleUsage: She brought the books to the return desk.

help-desk.definition: A counter where library staff answer questions and help visitors find resources.
help-desk.exampleUsage: Ask at the help desk if you cannot find a book.

archive.definition: A collection of records kept for future reference.
archive.exampleUsage: The archive holds old photographs and letters.

reading.definition: Looking at words in a book or other text.
reading.exampleUsage: Reading helps her learn new words.

borrowing.definition: Taking a library item home for a limited time and returning it later.
borrowing.exampleUsage: Borrowing books is free with a library card.

returning.definition: Bringing a borrowed library item back after using it.
returning.exampleUsage: Returning books on time helps other readers.

searching.definition: Looking for information by entering words or questions.
searching.exampleUsage: She is searching the catalog for a history book.

studying.definition: Reading carefully with intent to remember.
studying.exampleUsage: The students are studying quietly at the tables.

browsing.definition: Looking through books or shelves without searching for one specific title.
browsing.exampleUsage: He spent an hour browsing the new books.

reserving.definition: Asking the library to hold a book so you can borrow it later.
reserving.exampleUsage: Reserving the book means she can collect it when it is available.

photocopying.definition: The process of making paper copies of documents using a photocopier.
photocopying.exampleUsage: The library provides photocopying for permitted materials.

typing.definition: The action of entering words with a keyboard.
typing.exampleUsage: He is typing a search term into the catalog.

whispering.definition: Speaking very quietly so that other people in the library are not disturbed.
whispering.exampleUsage: The children were whispering in the reading room.

library-card.definition: A card that shows you have permission to use the library.

barcode-scanner.definition: An electronic device that reads printed barcodes to identify library items or records.
barcode-scanner.exampleUsage: The librarian scanned the book with a barcode scanner.

stamp.definition: A small tool used to print an official mark on a library item or paper.
stamp.exampleUsage: The librarian used a stamp to mark the return date.

bookmark.definition: A marker (a piece of paper or ribbon) placed between the pages of a book to mark the reader's place.
bookmark.exampleUsage: She placed a bookmark between the pages.

book-cover.definition: The protective outer part of a book that shows its title and often a picture.
book-cover.exampleUsage: The book cover shows a bright picture of the sea.

label.definition: A brief description given for purposes of identification.

catalog.definition: A searchable list of the books and other items held by a library.
catalog.exampleUsage: He searched the catalog for books about space.

computer.definition: An electronic device used to search the catalog, read, or write.
computer.exampleUsage: She used the computer to search for a book.

printer.definition: A machine that produces paper copies of documents or pictures.
printer.exampleUsage: He printed his assignment using the library printer.

scanner.definition: A device that turns a paper image or document into a digital file.
scanner.exampleUsage: The scanner was used during the activity.

librarian.definition: A person who works in or manages a library.
librarian.exampleUsage: The librarian helped him find a book.

assistant.definition: A person who contributes to the fulfillment of a need or furtherance of an effort or purpose.
assistant.exampleUsage: The assistant returned the books to their shelves.

volunteer.definition: A person who freely helps without being paid.

reader.exampleUsage: The reader sat quietly with a book.

student.definition: A person who studies at a school.

researcher.definition: A person who studies a subject carefully to discover or check information.
researcher.exampleUsage: The researcher examined old newspapers in the library.

author.definition: A person who writes a book, story, or other written work.
author.exampleUsage: The author signed her new book at the library.

storyteller.exampleUsage: The storyteller read a tale to the children.
storyteller.definition: A person who tells a story.

guard.definition: A person who watches over the library and helps keep people and property safe.
guard.exampleUsage: The guard checked the entrance before closing.

cleaner.definition: A person who cleans the library and keeps its rooms tidy.
cleaner.exampleUsage: The cleaner wiped the tables after closing time.
